forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, ℓ with 0 ≤ k, ℓ ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose ℓ]_q is a polynomial in q, then it has only nonnegative coefficients.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329110006_654a633e
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and 0 <= j <= floor(r (b - a) / 2). Put I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. For each positive integer d, define M_d(u,v) := |{m in Z : u < m <= v and d divides m}|, and assume M_d(r+a,r+b) >= M_d(a,b) for every positive integer d. Let X_j be the set of pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, |lambda| denotes the sum of the elements of lambda, and |lambda| + sum_{s in S} (r + s) = j. Then there exists an involution iota_j : X_j -> X_j such that: (1) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S',lambda') != (S,lambda), then |S'| is congruent to |S| + 1 modulo 2; and (2) if iota_j(S,lambda) = (S,lambda), then |S| is even.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329092547_6a64d34a
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

forbidden_claims.label: lem_20260329074016_d9949d95
forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let a, b, r be integers with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0. Define P_{a,b,r}(q) := product_{i=a+1}^{b} ((1 - q^(r+i)) / (1 - q^i)), with empty product equal to 1. Assume that for every positive integer d one has floor((r+b)/d) - floor((r+a)/d) >= floor(b/d) - floor(a/d). Then P_{a,b,r}(q) is a polynomial in Z[q], and every coefficient of P_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative.

payload.statement_nl: Let X be a finite set, and let p : X -> {0,1} be a function. Assume that the number of elements x in X with p(x) = 0 is at least the number of elements x in X with p(x) = 1. Then there exists a map iota : X -> X such that iota(iota(x)) = x for every x in X, and such that: if iota(x) != x, then p(iota(x)) = 1 - p(x); and if iota(x) = x, then p(x) = 0.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let
Z := {x in X : p(x) = 0}
and
O := {x in X : p(x) = 1}.
Because p maps X into {0,1}, every element of X lies in exactly one of Z or O. Thus X = Z ∪ O and Z ∩ O = ∅.

Since X is finite, the subsets Z and O are finite. Write
O = {o_1, ..., o_m},
Z = {z_1, ..., z_n},
for some integers m,n >= 0. The hypothesis says that the number of zero-labeled elements is at least the number of one-labeled elements, so n >= m.

Now define a map iota : X -> X as follows:
- for 1 <= i <= m, set iota(o_i) = z_i;
- for 1 <= i <= m, set iota(z_i) = o_i;
- for m < j <= n, set iota(z_j) = z_j.

This is well-defined because O and Z are disjoint, and every element of X is either some o_i or some z_j.

We check that iota is an involution.
- If x = o_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(z_i) = o_i = x.
- If x = z_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(o_i) = z_i = x.
- If x = z_j with m < j <= n, then iota(iota(x)) = iota(z_j) = z_j = x.
Hence iota(iota(x)) = x for every x in X.

Next, suppose iota(x) != x. Then x is in one of the first two cases above.
- If x = o_i, then iota(x) = z_i, so
  p(iota(x)) = p(z_i) = 0 = 1 - 1 = 1 - p(o_i) = 1 - p(x).
- If x = z_i with 1 <= i <= m, then iota(x) = o_i, so
  p(iota(x)) = p(o_i) = 1 = 1 - 0 = 1 - p(z_i) = 1 - p(x).
Thus whenever iota(x) != x, we have p(iota(x)) = 1 - p(x).

Finally, if iota(x) = x, then x cannot be any o_i and cannot be any z_i with 1 <= i <= m; therefore x = z_j for some j with m < j <= n. Hence p(x) = 0.

So iota is an involution on X, every moved point is matched with a point of opposite label, and every fixed point has label 0. This is exactly the required conclusion.
result_payload.proof_summary: Partition X into zero-labeled and one-labeled elements. Since there are at least as many zeros as ones, list the one-labeled elements as o_1,...,o_m and the zero-labeled elements as z_1,...,z_n with n>=m, pair each o_i with z_i, and fix the remaining z_j. The resulting map is an involution; moved points switch labels, and fixed points are exactly the unpaired zero-labeled elements.
